text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- Albanian opposition disappointed after the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said it will send only 400 monitors to oversee the June 29 elections.
- Leaders of so-called committees of public salvations in southern Albania rejected calls to disband the committees, saying they were needed to safeguard ballot boxes during the elections.
- Opposition parties turned down a proposal by the Democratic Party on a social pact, saying they wanted the state of emergency to be lifted first.
- The Democratic Party is almost nonexistent in Vlore and several other southern towns.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino asked parliamentary speaker Pjeter Arbnori to summon parliament to consider lifting the state of emergency. Parliament was dissolved last week by President Sali Berisha.
- The United States stepped up pressure on Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano to persuade him to take part in the elections, a Greek newspaper is quoted as saying.
ALBANIA
- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos will visit Albania next week to meet President Berisha, Premier Fino and Greek troops, stationed in Albania as part of a multinational force.

- The international community is willing to provide maximum help to Albania but the destiny of the country lies in its own hands, Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told an Albanian delegation in Rome.
- An OSCE advance team for monitoring elections has started working.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The domestic currency, the lek, continues to lose ground against the dollar. The dollar is currently quoted at 190 leks, up from 165 last week.
- Four rightist parties joined forces in a bid to oust President Berisha from politics.
- Prime Minister Fino left for The Hague to participate in the 50 anniversary of the Marshall Plan.
ALBANIA
- Berisha voiced his concern to Prime Minister Fino over the sacking of the heads of financial institutions. Fino assured him the practice would end.
- An Albanian dissident wants Berisha to change the composition of the central electoral commission after discovering the name of his former persecutor on the list.
INDEPENDENT
- Qemal Disha, the Insurance Institute director, has refused to step down after he was sacked by the Socialist Finance Minister Arben Malaj and has taken the matter to court.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- You have to defeat communists, Italian rightist parties told visiting Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu.

- The Democratic Party-led Union for Democracy is poised to win 55 percent of votes in the election, while the Rebellion Front, a term coined to depict the Socialist-led opposition, some 24 percent, a poll shows.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- The Socialist Party is a responsible force of the future, Socialist chairman Fatos Nano told an electoral rally in Tirana. He said Albania would not find peace with Berisha.
- Was an attack by members of the national guard of President Sali Berisha on a military hospital in Tirana a test for a coup d'etat, the paper asks.
